title: Real Hardware for SENSE
description: Back to Module 1's three boxes — except this time, box one has actual parts wired to it.

content.value: Module 1 taught you the sense-think-act loop as an idea. Modules 3 through 6 gave ARIA power, a brain, and the ability to move. This module fills in the last missing piece: real parts that turn the physical world into the numbers her brain needs.

SENSE            THINK              ACT
ultrasonic   -->  ESP32 controller --> motor driver --> wheels
IR sensors        (Module 4)          (Module 5)
(this module)

By the end of this module, ARIA can answer two questions no amount of programming alone could answer for her: "how far away is that wall?" and "is the floor under me light or dark?" Everything from here on — obstacle avoidance, line following, the projects ahead — depends on those two questions having real, honest answers.
Two Sensors, Two Very Different Jobs

This module covers two workhorse sensors: an ultrasonic distance sensor (bounces sound off things ahead) and IR line sensors (read light and dark directly beneath the chassis). They answer completely different questions, and you'll build a real behaviour — line following — out of the second one before the module ends.
Every sensor you'll ever meet does the same fundamental job: turn some physical quantity — distance, light, sound, heat — into a number a controller can read. The parts differ; that job never does.
Key takeaway: this module gives ARIA real sensors for the SENSE step of the loop — an ultrasonic sensor for distance, and IR sensors for reading the floor beneath her.

quiz.question: What job do ARIA's ultrasonic and IR sensors both share, despite working completely differently?
options: Turning a physical quantity into a number the controller can read
quiz.explain: Every sensor's fundamental job is the same: convert something physical into a number — only the physical quantity and the method differ.

quiz.question: Which two questions does this module let ARIA answer for the first time?
options: What colour is the wall, and what time is it?
How far away is that wall, and is the floor light or dark?
How fast is the motor spinning, and how much battery is left?
quiz.explain: Ultrasonic answers the distance question; IR line sensors answer the light/dark floor question — the two sensors this module covers.
